Option A: CSS-variable-driven theming with Tailwind v4 `@theme` tokens. Tailwind v4 supports defining custom colors via `@theme` and using them as `bg-surface` etc. But rewriting all classes is huge.

Option B: A pragmatic approach used widely: add a `data-theme="light"` attribute on `document.documentElement` (or a `.light` class on root container), and add CSS overrides in `index.css` for the commonly used utility patterns... but utility classes are numerous and fine-grained (`bg-white/[0.04]`, `border-white/10`, `text-slate-500`, `bg-slate-950/70`, etc.). Overriding each is impractical.

Option C: CSS variable remapping trick: Tailwind v4 maps many of its color utilities to CSS variables (`--color-white`, `--color-slate-500`, etc.). Actually, in Tailwind v4, colors used with opacity modifiers like `bg-white/[0.04]` compile to `color-mix(in oklab, var(--color-white) 4%, transparent)`. If we redefine `--color-white` and `--color-slate-*` etc. under a `[data-theme="light"]` scope... that would change white to something light-ish, but "white" is used for text too — remapping white to dark would invert text/background correctly? That's hacky: `text-white` on dark bg → remap `--color-white` to dark gray → text becomes dark on light bg. And `bg-white/[0.04]` would become a dark tint at 4% opacity — too subtle on light background; a 4% dark tint on white is nearly invisible.

Option D: Use Tailwind's built-in `dark:` variant with class strategy. The app would keep its dark classes as-is (they're the default), and we'd need to add `dark:` prefixed light classes everywhere — but Tailwind v4's `dark:` variant defaults to `prefers-color-scheme` media query; to use class strategy we'd need `@custom-variant dark (&:where(.dark, .dark *));`. Here the existing styles are the DARK styles, so we'd have to prefix every class with light overrides — that's a huge diff across every component.

Better: invert the strategy. Keep existing dark classes as the default (they already ARE the dark styles), and add `light:` variant overrides (custom variant) for the light theme. That still requires adding overrides to every element that needs to change — a huge diff.

Option E (cleanest for this codebase): CSS-variable-based theming where we define semantic tokens and rewrite the hardcoded colors into token-based classes. That's the "right" way but a very large refactor of ~6 components with hundreds of class strings.
